title: ISRO Special
blurb: Chandrayaan, Mangalyaan, Aditya-L1 and India's journey to space

questions.question: What does ISRO stand for?
questions.fact: ISRO was founded in 1969 and is headquartered in Bengaluru.

questions.question: India's Mars Orbiter Mission is popularly known as…
questions.fact: 'Mangal' is the Hindi name for Mars.

questions.question: Which is India's first space mission dedicated to studying the Sun?
questions.fact: 'Aditya' is a Sanskrit name for the Sun.

questions.question: The Chandrayaan missions explore…
questions.fact: 'Chandra' means Moon and 'yaan' means vehicle or craft.

questions.question: Who is known as the father of the Indian space programme?
questions.fact: Chandrayaan's lander 'Vikram' is named in honour of Dr Vikram Sarabhai.

questions.question: On 23 August 2023, Chandrayaan-3 made India the first country to land near which part of the Moon?
questions.fact: India became only the fourth nation ever to achieve a soft landing on the Moon.

questions.question: What was the name of Chandrayaan-3's lander?
questions.fact: The lander Vikram carried the six-wheeled rover Pragyan, meaning 'wisdom'.

questions.question: What was India's first satellite, launched in 1975?
questions.fact: Aryabhata was named after the 5th-century Indian mathematician and astronomer.

questions.question: Mangalyaan made India the first nation in the world to reach Mars orbit…
questions.fact: It reached Mars orbit on 24 September 2014 at a famously low cost.

questions.question: ISRO's main launch site, the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, is located at…
questions.fact: Sriharikota is an island off the coast of Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: Gaganyaan is ISRO's programme to…
questions.fact: The astronauts selected for India's human spaceflight programme are called 'Gaganyatris'.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian citizen to travel to space, in 1984?
questions.fact: Asked how India looked from space, he famously answered 'Saare Jahan Se Achha'.

questions.question: Aditya-L1 observes the Sun from a halo orbit around which point?
questions.fact: From L1, about 1.5 million km away, Aditya can watch the Sun without any eclipses.

questions.question: What does PSLV stand for?
questions.fact: The PSLV launched both Chandrayaan-1 and Mangalyaan.

questions.question: Which Indian-born astronaut lost her life in the Space Shuttle Columbia disaster in 2003?
questions.fact: Kalpana Chawla was the first woman of Indian origin to go to space, in 1997.

questions.question: In 2017, how many satellites did ISRO launch on a single PSLV rocket — a world record at the time?
questions.fact: PSLV-C37 deployed all 104 satellites in about 18 minutes.

questions.question: Chandrayaan-1 (2008) helped discover evidence of what on the Moon?
questions.fact: NASA's Moon Mineralogy Mapper aboard Chandrayaan-1 detected the signature of water.

questions.question: The site where Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander touched down was named…
questions.fact: Tiranga Point marks where Chandrayaan-2's lander struck the Moon in 2019.

questions.question: In which year was Mangalyaan launched?
questions.fact: It launched on 5 November 2013 and spent about 300 days cruising to Mars.

questions.question: Which heavy-lift rocket launched Chandrayaan-3?
questions.fact: LVM3 was earlier called GSLV Mk III and is ISRO's most powerful operational rocket.

questions.question: India celebrates National Space Day on which date?
questions.fact: It marks the anniversary of Chandrayaan-3's landing in 2023.
